judged_text: createEvent selects the target calendar only via destinationCalendar.find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId) and falls back to 'primary', discarding destinationCalendar rows that carry an externalId but no matching credentialId. Hosts whose destinationCalendar row has externalId set but credentialId null or stale — including every destination handled by the no-credentialId else-branch of EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents — get the booking event, containing attendee emails, names and notes, silently inserted into their primary calendar instead of the configured destination, and a host with multiple Google credentials receives one duplicated event per credential; the pre-diff code honored destinationCalendar.externalId regardless of credential match.

Hosts whose destinationCalendar row has externalId set but credentialId null or stale — including every destination handled by the no-credentialId else-branch of EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents — get the booking event, containing attendee emails, names and notes, silently inserted into their primary calendar instead of the configured destination, and a host with multiple Google credentials receives one duplicated event per credential; the pre-diff code honored destinationCalendar.externalId regardless of credential match.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, `createEvent` now chooses `selectedCalendar` only via `calEventRaw.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId)?.externalId` and otherwise uses `"primary"` (`calendarId: selectedCalendar || "primary"`). Since `destinationCalendar` is now an array, any destination entry that has an `externalId` but a `null/undefined` (or stale) `credentialId` will not match and will silently fall back to the primary calendar, ignoring the configured `externalId`. This can happen in the `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` no-`credentialId` branch, which still calls `createEvent(c, event)` for all credentials of `destination.integration` without supplying an external id, relying on `event.destinationCalendar` to carry routing info. The pre-diff Google logic used `destinationCalendar.externalId` directly, so this is a behavior change that can mis-route event creation to the wrong calendar.
